answer: A grove of agents stays honest when each identity must lock a refundable bond before it can earn, like planting a juniper that only grows after seasons of verified work. A newcomer starts with a small ember of trust and must complete attested tasks before its reputation counts. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of bonds plus time, while a Sybil that misbehaves loses its bond, so fakery costs more than the reward it could steal.
